trust_decision.summary: The shared-mode API server decides whether HTTP request bodies may be unpickled unrestricted; at the pinned commit only /simple_execute with a nonce set uses the allowlisted RestrictedUnpickler, while /execute and the nonce-disabled branch call pickle.loads directly.

landing_point.why: The summary names 'Share Model' pickle RCE; share.py is the only file in manga_translator/mode with pickle.loads on request.body(), and /execute has no restriction at all.

fix_sites.entry_point: HTTP POST /simple_execute/{method_name} with nonce disabled (--nonce None)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: server/streaming.py:13 unpickles the worker's response stream inside the web server, so a solver can argue it is trusted internal traffic from a registered instance and the opposite direction from the advisory's request-body sink.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: The web server's internal client pickles {'image': PIL.Image, 'config': Config} to /execute and /simple_execute, and share.py pickles Context results back; the restricted unpickler must still accept PIL images, numpy arrays and manga_translator.config objects (replacing pickle with JSON or a builtins-only allowlist breaks the server-to-worker translate flow).

O6_input_shapes: pickle body on /simple_execute when nonce is disabled ('None')

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Web server unpickles the code-0 result chunk from a translator instance with plain pickle.loads (streaming translate endpoints)
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Data comes from a registered executor instance (registration is nonce-gated at server/main.py:46-48), i.e. internal and reverse direction from the advisory's request-body sink.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: different package (server/ vs manga_translator/mode/), reached via server/request_extraction.py:69-70

O8_uncovered_routes.route: RestrictedUnpickler allowlist admits the whole 'builtins' module and the 'manga_translator' package root, and find_class resolves dotted names, so the allowlist check on the module string does not bound the callable that comes back
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The guard already exists and the advisory is framed as 'missing restricted loads on /execute'; a solver who routes /execute through restricted_loads will treat the allowlist as already correct.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file as landing point (how-type, not where-type)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a further shared-mode route (e.g. a batch/status endpoint) that loads its body via pickle.loads
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Routes in this file are added ad hoc per call style (simple vs streaming) and each does its own body decoding.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a non-streaming counterpart that unpickles the /simple_execute response in server/sent_data_internal.py:30-32
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: fetch_data was previously pickle-based and was switched to JSON; a legacy pickle path in the client is plausible.

O9_family: insecure deserialization (CWE-502, Python pickle over HTTP)

O10_build.project_tests: test/ has render/translation tests only; no tests for manga_translator/mode/share.py or server/

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Replace pickle.loads at share.py:164 (and :144) with the existing restricted_loads, leaving the builtins/package-root allowlist and server/streaming.py:13 untouched.
